subject: Canary hold + temporary SLO offset request — Model 12r p95 surge (ClearWave)
messages:
From: Ops Team <ops@clearwave.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Park <lisa@clearwave.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Model 12r p95 spike impacting payment flows — request to pause canary and SLO offset

Hi Jasmine,

We started seeing a reproducible p95 latency spike on model=12r around 07:30 UTC this morning (affecting "authorize_payment" endpoint). The spike correlates with a canary ramp to 20% that completed at 07:15. Our SREs captured attached samples and a compressed trace slice (clearwave_latency_snaps_11-09-2026.zip).

Impact: briefly blocked a portion of customer payment retries; downstream queueing increased but rate-limited successfully. Business impact is limited for now but velocity of errors is trending upward.

Ask: Can Redwood hold the canary (stop any further ramp) and authorize a temporary SLO offset for 48 hours while we coordinate a rollback or new variant patch? We need explicit permission to divert canary traffic back to stable-12q and for Redwood to mark the event as an approved SLO exception (ClearWave deal DW-8721).

We can provide any additional logs or grant a read-only link to our dashboards.

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Senior SRE, ClearWave Analytics
ops@clearwave.ai

Attachments: clearwave_latency_snaps_11-09-2026.zip
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@clearwave.ai, lisa@clearwave.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:45:00 GMT
Subject: Re: Model 12r p95 spike impacting payment flows — request to pause canary and SLO offset

Thanks for the heads-up, Samir — and for the artifacts. I've pulled the trace and can confirm the p95 tail is driven by longer decode steps at sequence lengths ~1.4x the historical median.

Internal ask: Ben/Marcus/Monica — can we get an approval path to: 1) halt the canary progression immediately (no new traffic to 12r), 2) divert existing canary traffic back to stable-12q, and 3) register a provisional SLO offset for up to 48 hours while we triage? ClearWave is requesting the offset for customer-facing KPIs tied to payments.

Proposed operational constraints:
- Any diversion must preserve per-customer affinity for the next 2h
- We log the traffic shift event and annotate audit logs with the DW-8721 tag
- We limit the SLO offset to p95 only (no modifications to availability SLOs)

Ben — do you need legal/finance signoff for the documented SLO carveout for a strategic customer here? Monica — please prepare the communication template to send to ClearWave once we have a go/no-go. Marcus — engineering, can you confirm a backward switch path to stable-12q with zero config drift?

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, ops@clearwave.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 17:12:00 GMT
Subject: Re: Model 12r p95 spike impacting payment flows — request to pause canary and SLO offset

Jasmine — I approve holding the canary and diverting traffic back to stable-12q for ClearWave (DW-8721) under the proposed constraints. Finance/legal: this is a short-lived, documented SLO exception; we'll flag for post-incident review and potential usage credit if required.

Conditions:
- Engineering must run the rollback path in a dry-run and confirm no cache/kv-store incompatibilities before live diversion.
- Operations to capture a full audit trail and create an incident timeline entry (INF-4521).

Marcus — proceed with the rollback rehearsals. Monica — please draft the customer note: include the timeline, what we changed, expected behavior, and the contact for escalation.

Ben Carter
Sr. Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@clearwave.ai, lisa@clearwave.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 19:03:00 GMT
Subject: Re: Model 12r p95 spike impacting payment flows — request to pause canary and SLO offset

Confirming: engineering completed a dry-run rollback to stable-12q in the staging cluster at 18:30 UTC. No incompatibilities found with KV cache schema or tokenization artifacts. We'll coordinate a rolling diversion window at 19:15 UTC (expected 5–10 minutes to drain and re-route).

Monica — I added a minimal ops checklist to the linked incident (INF-4521). Monica, once you have the customer note, I'll trigger the divert and monitor p95 in real-time.

Also uploading the signed SLO-exception stub to the shared folder and initiating the DocuSign envelope for the temporary exception (link below).

Forwarded links:
- Incident: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4521
- DocuSign: https://docusign.com/envelope/0a1b2c3d

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
